incidents.victim: U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA)
incidents.vector: A CISA contractor (Nightwing) intentionally disabled GitHub's built-in secret-scanning protection and published a public 'Private-CISA' repository containing plaintext credentials, AWS GovCloud admin keys, RSA private keys, SSH keys, and configuration files for dozens of internal CISA systems dating back to November 2025.
incidents.impact: One of the most severe U.S. government credential leaks on record. Exposed keys granted administrative access to CISA GovCloud accounts, full read/write access to all CISA-IT GitHub repositories, and the ability to hijack CI/CD pipelines. Senate and House lawmakers have demanded answers; CISA is still rotating exposed credentials more than a week after notification. Researchers warned that adversaries monitoring GitHub's public commit feed may already have copied the data.

incidents.vector: Intrusion into NYC Health + Hospitals systems leading to bulk exfiltration of patient medical records and biometric data.
incidents.impact: At least 1.8 million people affected; attackers stole sensitive medical data plus biometric information including fingerprints and palm prints — data the victims cannot replace.

incidents.victim: Foxconn (Hon Hai Precision Industry) — North American factories
incidents.vector: The Nitrogen ransomware group (which previously used ALPHV and later forked Conti code) breached Foxconn's North American manufacturing environments, encrypted systems and exfiltrated data.
incidents.impact: Production disrupted at Foxconn factories across Mexico, Wisconsin, Ohio, Texas, Virginia and Indiana. Attackers claim 8 terabytes / 11 million files stolen, allegedly including confidential project files and drawings tied to Intel, Apple, Google, Dell and Nvidia. Foxconn says affected plants are 'resuming normal production.'

incidents.attacker: China — state-suspected espionage group (UAT-8616) plus 10+ other clusters including criminal groups
incidents.vector: Cisco disclosed CVE-2026-20182, a CVSS 10 authentication-bypass zero-day in Catalyst SD-WAN Controller/Manager that lets an unauthenticated attacker present as a trusted router and obtain admin access. Cisco Talos attributes ongoing exploitation to UAT-8616, the same actor that exploited CVE-2026-20127 for years. Separately, at least 10 other clusters are chaining CVE-2026-20133/20128/20122 (patched Feb 2026) using ZeroZenX Labs PoC code to drop XenShell, Godzilla, Behinder, Sliver, Mythic, AdaptixC2 and XMRig.
incidents.impact: Affects on-prem, cloud and FedRAMP deployments; a single compromised controller gives attackers the ability to reroute traffic, intercept communications, push malicious configs, or sever connectivity across an entire SD-WAN fabric. CISA added the bug to its KEV catalog. The seventh Cisco edge bug added to KEV in three months.

incidents.vector: Active exploitation of a previously undisclosed Microsoft Exchange zero-day vulnerability with no patch available at time of disclosure.
incidents.impact: On-premises Exchange servers globally are exposed; Microsoft and CISA urged emergency mitigations while a fix is developed. Exchange compromises typically enable mailbox harvesting, credential theft and lateral movement into Active Directory.

incidents.vector: Threat actor compromised an end-of-life F5 BIG-IP Virtual Edition (v15.1.201000, EOL Dec 2024) running in Azure, pivoted via SSH to an internal Linux host, then exploited an unpatched Atlassian Confluence server. Stole credentials from Confluence configuration files and chained Kerberos relay attacks (CVE-2025-33073, PetitPotam coercion) to attempt Active Directory compromise.
incidents.impact: Microsoft Defender researchers detailed a multi-domain attack chain that crossed network, SaaS and identity boundaries. Demonstrates how unpatched edge appliances become initial-access points enabling identity-system compromise in hybrid environments.

incidents.victim: Aerospace, defense and tech-sector targets in U.S., Israel, UAE and Middle East
incidents.attacker: Iran — state-sponsored espionage group (tracked as Screening Serpens / UNC1549)
incidents.vector: Spear-phishing impersonating airlines, hiring portals and video-conferencing apps delivered ZIP archives that side-loaded six new RAT variants in two malware families ('MiniUpdate' and 'MiniJunk V2'). Used AppDomainManager hijacking to disable .NET app security via legitimate config files; routed C2 through 3-5 Azure-hosted domains per target.
incidents.impact: Coordinated espionage campaigns aligned with the Middle East regional conflict that began Feb 28, 2026. Unit 42 attributes the activity with moderate-high confidence; samples surfaced from U.S., Israel, UAE and two additional Middle Eastern entities between Feb and Apr 2026.

incidents.victim: Government organizations in Belgium, Italy, Serbia, Spain, Poland and South Africa
incidents.attacker: China — state-suspected espionage group (tracked as Webworm)
incidents.vector: ESET documented a Chinese APT that has shifted from Asian to European targets, abusing Discord ('EchoCreep' backdoor) and Microsoft Graph / OneDrive ('GraphWorm' backdoor) for command-and-control, plus SoftEther VPN and custom SOCKS proxy tools (ChainWorm, SmuxProxy, WormFrp). Malware staged in GitHub repos and a compromised Amazon S3 bucket.
incidents.impact: Espionage access to multiple European government networks. Attackers use legitimate cloud services to blend into normal traffic, evading signature-based detection.

incidents.vector: FBI advisory on Kali365, a Telegram-based phishing-as-a-service ($250-$2,000) that captures legitimate Microsoft OAuth access and refresh tokens, bypassing MFA without ever stealing the password. Victims are tricked into completing Microsoft's legitimate device-login flow on the attacker's behalf using AI-generated lures impersonating Adobe, DocuSign and SharePoint.
incidents.impact: Hundreds of attacks observed since April 2026 (Arctic Wolf, Proofpoint, IBM, Huntress). Captured tokens enable persistent mailbox access, contact harvesting, lateral phishing, BEC keyword monitoring and admin actions; attackers install inbox rules to suppress security notifications and extend dwell time.

incidents.victim: Jacob Butler / KimWolf DDoS botnet operator
incidents.vector: Canadian authorities arrested 23-year-old Jacob Butler ('Dort') of Ottawa on a U.S. extradition warrant for operating KimWolf, an IoT botnet that infected over one million typically-firewalled devices (digital photo frames, web cameras, streaming boxes) and rented them as DDoS-for-hire infrastructure.
incidents.impact: KimWolf launched record-setting DDoS attacks measured at nearly 30 Tbps, issued 25,000+ attack commands, caused victim losses exceeding $1M each, and targeted IP ranges owned by the U.S. Department of Defense. Infrastructure for KimWolf and three sister botnets (Aisuru, JackSkid, Mossad) was seized in March 2026.

incidents.victim: Open-source software supply chain (hundreds of npm/JavaScript packages)
incidents.vector: After the original Shai-Hulud worm source code was publicly released, fresh 'Mini Shai-Hulud' clones spread across hundreds of open-source packages. A parallel attack also weaponized RubyGems packages as 'dead drops' for stolen data. Related: TanStack, Mistral AI and UiPath were hit in another supply-chain wave; the official Checkmarx Jenkins AST plugin and an OpenAI-impersonating Hugging Face repo (244K downloads) were also compromised with infostealers.
incidents.impact: Hundreds of packages compromised; the worms target developer credentials, API keys, cloud secrets, tokens and cryptocurrency wallets, then republish themselves through compromised maintainer accounts. Sustained pressure on the JavaScript/AI dev ecosystem.

incidents.victim: United Arab Emirates fuel storage infrastructure
incidents.vector: Cyber intrusions into UAE fuel-tank operational technology systems, expanding the cyber dimension of the regional conflict beyond Israel into Gulf states.
incidents.impact: Fuel tank breaches widen the geography of Iran's cyber offensive during the ongoing Iran war. Comes alongside a physical drone attack on the Barakah nuclear plant from Iraq, blamed on Iran-backed militias.

incidents.vector: Reported intrusion into Taiwan's bullet-train operational systems, exposing cybersecurity gaps in rail OT environments.
incidents.impact: Highlighted systemic weaknesses in rail-system cybersecurity; raises concern about adversary pre-positioning in transportation critical infrastructure.

incidents.victim: Energy firm in the South Caucasus
incidents.attacker: China — state-suspected espionage group (tracked as FamousSparrow)
incidents.vector: Long-running Chinese APT established persistent access at a South Caucasus energy company.
incidents.impact: Espionage foothold inside a regional energy operator; signals continued Chinese targeting of energy-sector intelligence in geopolitically sensitive regions.

incidents.victim: Government organizations in Poland and Ukraine
incidents.attacker: Russia — state-linked espionage group (tracked as FrostyNeighbor)
incidents.vector: Targeted intrusions by a Russia-aligned APT against government bodies in Poland and Ukraine.
incidents.impact: Continued Russian espionage pressure on NATO frontline states and Ukrainian government targets amid the ongoing war.

incidents.vector: Microsoft's May 2026 Patch Tuesday addressed 137 vulnerabilities, 31 rated critical, with no in-the-wild zero-days. Most severe: CVE-2026-41089 (Windows Netlogon stack overflow, unauthenticated RCE on domain controllers); CVE-2026-41096 (Windows DNS Client heap overflow, network-triggerable RCE); CVE-2026-42898 (Microsoft Dynamics 365 code injection, CVSS 9.9); plus criticals in Azure, Office, Word, SharePoint, Windows GDI and the Native WiFi driver.
incidents.impact: Domain-controller-class bugs require urgent patching; researchers expect AI-assisted exploit development to compress the patch window. CISA, NYDFS and NCSC concurrently issued guidance warning of a coming 'patch surge' driven by frontier-AI vulnerability discovery.

incidents.attacker: China — PRC government officials and Ministry of Foreign Affairs
incidents.vector: DOJ charged Arcadia Mayor Eileen Wang with acting as an illegal agent of the People's Republic of China. Wang and a co-conspirator (Yaoning 'Mike' Sun, already serving four years) operated the 'U.S. News Center' website, receiving and executing directives via WeChat from PRC officials — including a senior intelligence official (John Chen) — to post pro-PRC propaganda, including Xinjiang denial content.
incidents.impact: First sitting U.S. mayor publicly charged in this PRC influence network; Wang has agreed to plead guilty. Underscores PRC use of elected local officials and ostensibly local-language 'news' sites to launder state messaging into U.S. audiences.

incidents.vector: ShinyHunters claimed a second intrusion into Instructure following the earlier breach of its Canvas learning-management platform; the group had previously stolen Canvas data in an extortion standoff that Instructure said ended with the data being returned.
incidents.impact: Instructure customers — primarily schools and universities reliant on Canvas — face renewed exposure of student and faculty data. Congress is now pressing Instructure for answers following the Canvas outage and successive breaches; the incident has become a case study in K-12/higher-ed vendor concentration risk.
